summary: Tencent's HY-World 2.0, which the map lists as Hunyuan World 2.0, is a model that turns a sentence, a photograph, a set of photographs or a video into a three-dimensional place, and its whole argument is that the place should be a file rather than a film: where a video world model draws the next frame forever, this one runs once and hands you Gaussian splats, a fused mesh and a point cloud that an ordinary engine can open. Two halves sit in one repository. Reconstruction takes pictures and returns depth, surface normals, camera poses, intrinsics, points and splats in a single pass, and will take known cameras or depth as a prior. Generation makes a 360-degree panorama, parses it into a mesh and a navigation mesh, has a vision-language model plan collision-free camera routes through it, generates the views those routes would see, and fits a splat scene to the result. It is genuinely open in the sense that weights, code and a detailed report are published, and genuinely not open source: the licence excludes the European Union, the United Kingdom and South Korea, forbids using the outputs to improve any other model, and requires a separate grant above a million monthly users. For a standards audience the important part is what does not come out. Everything it writes is somebody else's format used as-is — splat and mesh PLY, the compressed SPZ form, a COLMAP model, a camera JSON — with no scene graph, no object identity, no units, no licence field, no signature and no statement that the place was manufactured rather than photographed. There is no specification of the output and no conformance test, and the documentation chapter for the generation pipeline reads coming soon. Two claims in the technical report describe a rendering platform called WorldLens, with image-based lighting, collision and character control; it is not in the repository or the open-source plan, so the interactive, lit, walkable world the report shows cannot be reproduced from the release, and the rows here are scored on what was published.

coverage.note: It rasterizes, but only Gaussians. The trainer and both viewers draw the scene through a modified copy of the gsplat CUDA rasterizer, with render modes for colour, depth, alpha and normals; there is no render graph, no pass structure and no path for ordinary triangle meshes, which are exported for other engines to draw.
